description: A constructor parameter written this.name declares the parameter and assigns the property of the same name
self.name is the same prefix, and the constructor body can read both the parameter and the property
code:
class Box(self.width, self.height):
    this.area = width * height
    this.square = this.width == this.height
box = Box(3, 3)
[box.area, box.square]

description: A prefixed parameter keeps its type annotation and literal default, and a label binds it by name
code:
class Account(this.owner: str, this.balance: int = 0)
a = Account(balance=50, owner="ana")
b = Account("bo")
[a.owner, a.balance, b.owner, b.balance]

description: A final rest parameter with the prefix stores the list of the remaining arguments, empty when there are none
code:
class Playlist(this.name, ...this.songs)
mix = Playlist("mix", "intro", "outro")
quiet = Playlist("quiet")
[mix.songs, quiet.songs]

description: An init method written in the class body takes prefixed parameters and is adopted as the constructor
The prefixed assignments run before a leading super call, so a parent that assigns the same property wins
A class-level rule reads the properties that prefixed parameters assign and stays live
code:
class Order(this.qty, this.price)
$Order.total = $Order.qty * $Order.price
order = Order(2, 5)
order.qty = 3
order.total

description: A parameter without the prefix still creates no property
